Interactive · click a stage

Six stages, one question each

TS Studio is the Woods troubleshooting workbook bound to this simulator: one page per stage.

    Each stage answers one question before the next may start; red sub-steps are the MUST set of the workshop.

    Part 1 · the link bar on the Systematic problem solving tab

    Part 1 · Case & team page

    The workbook already knows V-101

    Part 1 · summary

    What part 1 settled

    • Six stages, Problem to Look back, plus a Review of fundamentals.
    • Four copies: the tab, its own window, a shared link, an offline HTML file.
    • Only the tab pulls simulator data by itself; the others read CSV files.
    • Workshop shows the MUST sub-steps; Full shows every one.
    • The V-101 pack brings tags, cases, fishbone branches and drawings.

    Part 2 · Stage by stage

    What do I fill in at each stage, and where does the simulator feed it?

    Part 2 · the plan

    From the first data to the closed ledger

    1. Data & evidencelive pulls in the tab, CSV files elsewhere
    2. Engage, Define, Exploreurgency, the problem statement, the hypotheses
    3. Planscreen hypotheses with S/D/N, cost every test
    4. Do it, Look backthe plant test, its verdict, what changes for good

    Part 2 · OTS data & evidence, inside the tab

    Three pulls, no files

    Every stage after Stage 0 argues from data, so the data comes first.

    Interactive · the standalone copies read files

    Which CSV loads as what?

    The workbook decides by the header row: tag and value_now make a snapshot; anything with a time column is a run.

    Interactive · stages 1 and 2 of TE-1

    Is it urgent, and what exactly is wrong?

    Decide run, safe-park or shut down first; then state the problem with numbers and no cause.

    Interactive · stage R and stage 3 of TE-1

    Fundamentals, fishbone, hypotheses

    Write each hypothesis as "if … then we should observe …" so the data can deny it.

    Interactive · 4.3 click a cell: S → D → N

    Screen the hypotheses against the evidence

    One D (a fact that contradicts it) kills a hypothesis; the survivors go to the plant-test plan.

    Part 2 · 4.6 the plant-test plan

    Each test names what would kill a hypothesis

    Interactive · 4.8 and 6.4 the cost ledger

    What did finding the cause cost?

    Off-spec oil is the line that grows with every minute: about five minutes of it cost more than all three tests.

    Interactive · 5.0 T-3 on the simulator, three seeded runs

    Restart P-105, or only add heat?

    Only the restart turns BS&W down: the control run with heat alone keeps rising, so the test confirms WH-1.

    Part 2 · stage 6 of TE-1

    Close the ledger, keep the lesson

    Part 2 · summary

    What part 2 settled

    • Pull run, snapshot and log after the case, each test and the fix.
    • The header row decides how a CSV file loads.
    • Decide the urgency first; state the problem with numbers, not causes.
    • One fact that denies a hypothesis kills it.
    • Every test is planned, costed and judged against its kill criterion.

    Part 3 · the hand-in

    Save, open, hand in

      Part 3 · summary

      What part 3 settled

      • TE-1 opens from Worked examples, or from its downloaded file.
      • It is a worked case for everyone, not a graded exercise.
      • The first alarm, not the loudest one, pointed to the cause.
      • Report and team slides come from the stages you filled.
      • Save a .woods.json file; it opens in any copy of the workbook.

      This deck

      Key Takeaways

      1

      Work the six stages in order; state the problem before you name a cause.

      2

      Pull the data after the case, every test and the fix, and label each set.

      3

      Kill hypotheses with facts, then test the survivors against a stated criterion.

      4

      Cost every test and every minute off spec in the ledger.

      5

      Save the .woods.json file often; it is your hand-in.
